summary: Read-only review complete. Two authorization races remain. No edits, builds, tests, or network access.

findings.title: Recovery-code replacement does not invalidate pending recovery-code proof
findings.detail: The captured epoch/password/TOTP snapshot survives recovery-code regeneration unchanged. second-factor.ts:40-43 deletes the previous code rows, but verifySecondFactor returns only a boolean. A request paused after consuming an old recovery code can therefore resume after another regeneration and create a session, earn step-up, accept an invite, or replace the newly issued recovery codes. The proposed snapshot checks cannot detect this replacement.
findings.fix:
Recovery-code proof additionally carries a server-internal receipt containing the consumed `admin_recovery_code.id`, its `admin_user_id` and the persisted `used_at` returned by the successful atomic consumption. Native login, native step-up, existing-account credential-based staff-invite acceptance and recovery-code regeneration carry this receipt alongside the captured epoch/password/TOTP snapshot. Under the final `admin_user FOR UPDATE` lock, before any rehash, session insertion, step-up write, invite claim or recovery-code replacement, require that exact consumed recovery-code row and timestamp still exist for the locked owner. A missing or changed receipt rejects the pending operation using its existing credential-failure response. Never accept this receipt from the client. Recovery-code replacement and deletion, including standalone helpers, acquire the owner lock before touching recovery-code rows; when the credential advisory lock is used, acquire it before the owner lock. Transactional factor consumption remains inside its caller's owner-locked transaction. Regeneration need not invalidate independent passkeys, TOTP proof or already-completed step-ups. Add deterministic real-route tests pausing each recovery-code-authenticated consumer after consumption, regenerating the codes through another session, then resuming: no session, step-up, membership or replacement recovery-code set may be committed. In the regeneration case, the newer returned codes must remain usable. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps.

Deterministic concurrency controls (§8) race each new transaction against each row above and staff-invite acceptance in both orders.

findings.title: Customer logout bypasses the lock protecting session-bound artifact consumption
findings.detail: Customer passkey transactions only SELECT the calling session. POST /v1/shop/auth/logout calls deleteSession, which deletes it without locking the customer (auth/session.ts:157-158; routes/auth.ts:734). Logout can therefore commit after the proposed live-session read but before the artifact claim and credential mutation. The owner lock does not enforce the document's revocation guarantee against this path.
findings.fix: Order for every new passkey transaction: **owner row `FOR UPDATE` → (admin only) calling session row `FOR UPDATE` → artifact claim → credential row `FOR UPDATE` → writes.** Customer passkey transactions never lock or delete a session row: they re-read the session with a plain `SELECT` under the customer lock, requiring the same customer and store, `expires_at > clock_timestamp()` and the legacy-expiry rule, without idle checks or renewal. Every customer-session revocation must therefore acquire that same customer lock before deleting sessions. Restructure `POST /v1/shop/auth/logout` and `deleteSession`: identify the customer using a non-renewing lookup constrained by token hash and resolved store, lock that customer `FOR UPDATE`, then delete only the session matching that token hash, customer and store on the same connection. Preserve CSRF validation, cookie clearing and idempotent success for an absent session. Password reset, password change, email-change consumption and erasure retain their customer-first revocation order. Hold the customer lock through each artifact claim and authorized effect. Add deterministic real-route races between customer logout and management-grant issuance, mailbox confirmation, grant consumption and registration verification: when logout wins, no artifact is consumed and no credential mutation succeeds; when the authenticated operation wins, logout cannot commit until that operation finishes. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps.
